statement: A body cannot be registered as a corporate entity under the Act if there is no direct provision or intent to incorporate it.
supporting_quote: (1) The common characteristics of a corporation are a distinctive name, a common seal and perpetuity of existence. As a Rule the contracts of a corporation must be under seal of the corporation. Per Shiranee Bandaranayake, J. "It is evident that for the establishment of an institution as a body corporate clear provision to that effect should be provided in the enactment". (2) In the absence of any direct provision or any intent to incorporate, it is evident that the Sri Lanka Transport Board under the present Act cannot be registered as a body Corporate

statement: The burden of proving prescriptive title falls on the defendant where the legal title is in the plaintiff.
supporting_quote: It is settled law that where the legal title is in the plaintiff the burden of proving prescriptive title falls on the defendant (Siyanaris Vs Jayasinghe Udeni De Silva 52 NLR 289, Juliana Hamine Vs. Don Thomas 59 NLR 546, Sirajudeen and two others Vs. Abbas 1994 (2) SLR 365).

statement: A Magistrate cannot assume jurisdiction to hear and determine a case under Section 66 of the Primary Courts' Procedure Act if a civil action is pending in a District Court, unless there is a breach of peace.
supporting_quote: If the mere institution of a suit in a civil Court is sufficient to divest the Magistrate of his jurisdiction, the whole purpose of Section 62 will be defeated. A scheming party will be enabled to play hide and seek

statement: A party cannot claim ownership of land that has been vested in the Land Reform Commission under the Land Reform Law.
supporting_quote: By the time the plaintiff gave evidence before the District Court on 14.12.1972 and when the District Judge pronounced the Judgment on 24.01.1973, the land had been vested in the Land Reform Commission by operation of law, i.e. by operation of section 3 of the Land Reform Law, No. 1 of 1972, which came into operation on 26.08.1972.

statement: When a defendant says that the land described in the plaint is only a portion of a larger land or vice versa, the Court has authority to re-issue a commission to another surveyor.
supporting_quote: Since the introduction of partition law in this country, when a defendant says that the land described in the plaint is only a portion of a larger land or vice versa, the Court has authority to re-issue a commission to another surveyor.

statement: A party can claim their rights when partitioning land according to the Partition Act, even if the plaintiff's stands have changed over time.
supporting_quote: all parties can claim their rights when partitioning lot 1 and 2 of the preliminary plan, according to the partition act.

statement: A person who has entered into possession of land as a licensee is presumed to continue to possess it in the same capacity, and to claim prescriptive title, the licensee must prove an overt and unequivocal act manifesting his intention to possess adversely to the true owner.
supporting_quote: Where a licensee claims that his original possession has later become adverse, he must prove of the manifestation of his intention to possess adversely to the true owner by what is sometimes referred to as an ‘overt unequivocal act’.

statement: A co-owner who has made improvements should be allotted the portion which contains the improvements, provided it does not cause substantial injustice to the other co-owners.
supporting_quote: a co,owner who has made improvements should be allotted the portion which contains the improvements, provided it does not cause substantial injustice to the other co,owners

statement: A party invoking the provisions of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance to defeat an adverse claimant to immovable property must establish a starting point for their acquisition of prescriptive rights.
supporting_quote: Where a party invokes the provisions of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance in order to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property, the burden of proof rests squarely and fairly on him to establish a starting point for his or her acquisition of prescriptive rights.

statement: A party invoking the provisions of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property must establish a starting point for their acquisition of prescriptive rights.

statement: The Plaintiff can obtain prescriptive title by establishing long and continued possession of the disputed land.
supporting_quote: It is crystal clear that the long and continued possession of the disputed land to obtain prescriptive title was established by evidence.

statement: The formalities required to be observed when transferring and/or selling a land or other immovable property as laid down in Section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance were not followed when executing the deed.
supporting_quote: In terms of Section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance a sale or transfer of land has to be in writing signed by two or more witnesses before a Notary, duly attested by the Notary and the witnesses. If this is not done, the document and its contents cannot be used in evidence [Samarakaan v. Gunasekera and Another (2011) 1 SrLL.R. 149].

statement: A court in a partition action can only investigate title within the limits of pleadings, admissions, points of contest, evidence both documentary and oral.
supporting_quote: Court cannot go on a voyage of discovery tracing the title and finding the shares of the corpus for them. Otherwise parties will tender their pleadings and expect the Court to do their work and their Attorneys-at-Law's work, for them to get title to those shares in the corpus.

statement: A court cannot rewrite a contract entered into between parties.
supporting_quote: Court cannot rewrite a contract entered into between parties.

statement: A District Judge trying a partition action is under a sacred duty to investigate into title on all material that is forthcoming at the commencement of the trial.
supporting_quote: In the exercise of this sacred duty to investigate title, a Trial Judge cannot be found fault with for being too careful in his investigation.

statement: A person who has been summoned in terms of section 6 of the Act can only establish that he is in possession or occupation of the land upon a valid permit or other written authority of the State granted in accordance with any written law and that such permit or authority is in force and not revoked or otherwise rendered invalid.
supporting_quote: A person who has been summoned in terms of section 6 of the Act can only establish that he is in possession or occupation of the land upon a valid permit or other written authority of the State granted in accordance with any written law and that such permit or authority is in force and not revoked or otherwise rendered invalid.

statement: The Court of Appeal can set aside an interlocutory or final decree in a partition action by way of revision and restitutio in integrum where a miscarriage of justice has occurred.
supporting_quote: The powers of the Court of Appeal by way of revision and restitutio in integrum shall not be affected by the provisions of this Subsection.

statement: An assessment is not time-barred if it is issued after a departmental computation of the amount of tax with which a particular assessee is considered to be chargeable.
supporting_quote: Such rejection was possible only after a departmental computation of the amount of tax with which a particular assessee is considered to be chargeable.

statement: The burden of seeking and getting evidence before court, in the course of investigation of title to the land sought to be partitioned by parties before Court, prior to deciding what share should go to which party is more the duty of the judge than the contesting parties.
supporting_quote: The burden of seeking and getting evidence before court, in the course of investigation of title to the land sought to be partitioned by parties before Court, prior to deciding what share should go to which party is more the duty of the judge than the contesting parties.

statement: In a partition case, it is incumbent on the judge to investigate into the title of each party before he arrives at a determination.
supporting_quote: In a partition case, it is incumbent on the judge to investigate into the title of each party before he arrives at a determination [Chandrasena v. Piyasena and Others (1999) 3 SrLL.R. 201] and it would be the prime duty of the trial judge to carefully examine and investigate the actual rights and titles to the land sought to be partitioned [Sopinona v. Pitipanaarachchi and Two Others (2010) 1 SrLL.R. 87].
